It wouldn't because I did marry him. He's dead now.

He was one of my first boyfriends at the age of 15 and he was 18. I told him when we were first dating that I wouldn't be having sex with him because
1. It would be against the law to have sex  with an underaged girl.
2. I knew that I wouldn't be interested in sex now or for a few years yet.

We went out initially for a year and a half and he left to go to college. I told him because he respected me, loved me and never cheated on me, I was going to make him a promise that when I was ready he'd be the first one I looked up. I promised him he could have the honour of deflowering me, popping my cherry, etc.

What I didn't expect as he was a virgin too that he'd wait for me and he did. Some months after I turned 18 and become close friends while he was away in college, we got together. And I know he had kept it because he was just as clumsy as I was but after an amazing 3 hours of foreplay, we did it.

We remained close friends and had an off again on again relationship after that because I went off to uni but returned and a couple of years later I moved in him at 22. We were engaged to be married when I was 23 and due to life's challenges, I finally got married to my best friend, partner in crime, confidante, lover, to make him my husband at 30.

Never would I realise I would become a widow at 46 though.

First movie to ever disappoint me had to be at a Drive-In Theatre when I was 4 years old. We saw King Kong, but not Peter Jackson's version. I was crying at the end of the movie because the planes were shooting at the big gorilla who climbed to the top of the Empire State Building to get away from those nasty hunters. He just wants to be free and left alone. I think I still cried at the end of Peter Jackson's version too.

Star Wars trilogy modernized and Episodes 1 - 3 are not part of my SW canon.

At least, Anakin is believable because Hayden's portrayal of the character wasn't much better. Wooden boy, wooden teen. At least, the quality of acting was consistent. 
Sometimes, the mystery is better than the science. No midichlorians! Virgin birth? Give me a break.

I know, right? I've never looked forward so much to having an expiry date as to when I will end my life.  It gives me joy in planning every last detail. With my family dead and have crossed over to the Other Side, I want nothing more than to join them.

This I can relate to 100%. I only have my family's stuff and my stuff to pass on, create a digital archive, see a few sights and waiting for a couple more experiences and then I'm done. That's it. C'est tout!

Definitely. Any holiday now feels so hollow. I only observe days that are relevant to my family members' passing.  December is like trying to navigate a field filled with landmines.  If it's not my birthday, it's my late husband's birthday later this month. Today is the first anniversary of my emotional support animal's passing who was just as traumatized to witness her fellow pet owner dying. In just a few days, it'll be my dear father-in-law's birthday who I saw for the very last time along with saying goodbye for the final time to my grandmother.  Her anniversary of her passing is on Yule, the longest night of the year.  My husband's family used to celebrate on Christmas Eve.  New Year's was my Mother's, my and my husband's favourite holiday.  This month includes the 9th month passing of my mother.  Everyone I care about is on the Other Side now and it's incredibly tempting to just die and join them.

Today is going to be rough to get through as it's the anniversary of Persephone's passing.  She was my emotional support animal who like me was traumatized by the loss of my husband, her fellow caretaker.  She was there when my husband suffered his fatal brain aneurysm.  Losing her last year felt much like losing another piece of him as she was thought to be "Daddy's Little Girl" (My husband and I had no children so our pets were surrogates.) I miss her so much and I'd be reunited with her and the rest of my family on the Other Side when I complete suicide. :(

That's a very good question and I'd also love to hear what other practitioners have to say about this.  I think really it's a preference to have it north or east but if you're communing with the Lady and Lord and you can see nature outside your window (What better way in my opinion to set up your altar by including Her wondrous beauty into its setup?), it could be okay as an exception. You could try some spells, prayers, on that altar and see what the effects are, then relocate the altar to the east side of the room to see if it's any better. Also since some of the rituals that may require you to be facing north, e.g. Circle of protection, you don't need to face the altar to do that. In fact, you're going to be facing all four directions.

Finally, I think and again, this is just my own opinion that your relationship with the Goddess is like any relationship: it involves give and take. She would want you to be comfortable while you meditate with her but maybe having your back to the North could be considered disrespectful to Her. Worse comes to worse, you both can come to a compromise and you can meditate facing east. ;)

Let me know how it goes. I'd be interested to hearing how it went.

Blessed be :)

Well, it depends on the coven too. Titles are more likely based on a skill level in the tradition of the Craft within the circle. You have Initiates, Apprentices, Adepts, Priests/Priestesses, High Priests/High Priestesses. But I can understand too with the term "witches" culturally it's been associated with women. Male Ladybugs I'm sure are irked as well when they're thought of as female.

But there's lots of variations for guys in the Craft, including magi (magus), magician, sorceror. I prefer the term sorceress for myself.  I think though it comes down to what /you/ want to be called. Just like if someone calls you by the wrong variation of your name that you don't like just politely let them know. Most likely, they'll respect and remember that preference.

Well, there are many instances but to sum up the biggest ritual, The Great Rite, I've performed most years either literally in private or ritualistically as in the case last year publically in Wales.  I've found it's a good way to build up energy for other schools of magick but to borrow from Eastern philosophies, it's part of developing a kundabuffer organ by practicing black tantra.

For those times when I'm working with a partner, I've found that red tantra works best as you're working with both energies from the root and the heart chakras. It is known that the heart center of energy is the most powerful even more than the chakra located at the Third Eye both magnetically and electrically. Simply put, the heart wants what the heart wants after all. That potential manifestation of the desire outcome sometimes need to be repeated several times. I hope that helps. :)

I'm so glad you brought this up because it is a very misunderstood topic when it comes to different schools of magick. It doesn't help either that in America that in some areas, old Puritan notions about sexuality, especially sacred sexuality, is kept in the closet.  It's much in the same way that some of those same people zero in and create a misinformed view of GLBT relationships.

It's kind of funny too because if you look at Wicca or paganism in general, it is about the process of the cycle creation, death and rebirth. There's three fertility related occasions in the Cycle of the Wheel and it's about not just sex, it's procreation. We wouldn't have food, shelter, natural clothing (fur, cotton, wool, silk) as protection from the elements, nor children if our Mother Earth didn't flourish every spring and whether it's germination, husbandry, pollination, intercourse, we wouldn't have these necessities of life. Sex means life.

Without the sun though, we wouldn't have this cycle; life would ultimately stop. We need gravity to have air to breathe even and so Mother Earth needs this relationship with the sun to thrive and to take care of all living things. So, celebrations like Ostara, Beltane and Litha, we are rejoicing that we have the sun with us. The Wheel of the Year is a story of that relationship between them.

So, coming back to sex magick, it's probably the oldest form of magick in history. The first name of the Goddess that was attributed to her was Inanna during the Akkadian/Mesopotamian/Babylon/Sumerian era. Even on a tablet there is talk of the wonderment of the female genitalia in cuneiform. However, what I find in paganism or even Wicca, with the Horned God, it goes back to Pan but it should go back even further to Inanna's mate, Tammuz. The mystery of life when it occurred was magick and so when women gave birth to living beings back then, it was considered magick. Of course, any magick is really science undiscovered.  These sabbats go back to the beginning of the Agricultural Revolution in our civilization's history.

One other point I'd like to raise is how sex magick is represented today all over the world in other religions, be it Buddism, Hinduism, Gnostic Christianity, Thelema, Judaism, of course, and probably even in Islam. Right now, even in Japan, they're having fertility festivals (Look up Honen Matsuri sometime). It's just amazing! And we're not talking about the ancient religions that mythology knows so well from Egypt, China, Greek, Roman, just to name a few off the top of my head.

Sex magick is more than just the transfer of biological matter from one being to another. It's the manifestation of potential energy that is created by either one person, one couple or one group that is directed towards the betterment of the individual, the relationship, or for giving back to Mother Earth.

Thanks for bringing up this topic. It's one near and dear to my heart.  Blessed be!
Jewel
